# Varroa mite treatment

## Why I bother counting

Varroa destructor sits on the bees and in the sealed brood and carries deformed wing virus. You don't see it until it's too late, so the whole game is counting. Derek Yeo, our seasonal bee inspector for the Teign Valley Beekeepers, says "count, don't guess" at every meeting, and he's right.

## How I count

### Natural drop

Sticky white insert under the open mesh floor, slid in for 7 days, then counted with a magnifying glass and a pencil, ticking in a grid. Divide by 7 for the daily drop. The National Bee Unit threshold I go by: over 10 a day in May, over 6 a day in August, means treat.

### Alcohol wash

Only on the big hives, in July. Half a cup of bees from a brood frame (roughly 300), shaken in surgical spirit in the wash jar with the mesh lid. More than 9 mites = 3%, treat.

I don't like killing 300 bees for a number, so I only do it on Primrose and Bramble, which are strong enough not to notice.

## 2024 counts

| Hive | 10 May daily drop | 9 Aug daily drop | July wash |
|---|---|---|---|
| Primrose (H1) | 1.3 | 7.9 | 14 mites |
| Bramble (H2) | 0.6 | 3.1 | 5 mites |
| Hazel (H3) | 2.4 | 11.2 | not done |
| Ivy (H4, new 2024 nucleus) | 0.1 | 1.0 | not done |

Hazel was the worst, which matches the scruffy crumpled wings I saw on a few young bees in early August.

## What I used and when

### Summer: Apivar strips

Amitraz strips, two per brood box, between frames 3/4 and 7/8, in from 12 August to 23 September 2024 (6 weeks). Supers off first, of course. Bought from Thorne's, 10 strips for £29.95, batch AV-4410. Primrose, Hazel and Bramble treated; Ivy left alone with a drop of 1.0.

### Drone brood removal

In May and June put a shallow frame in Hazel's brood box so they draw drone comb on the bottom. Cut out the sealed drone brood every 3 weeks and fed it to the hens next door. Uncapped 50 cells on 4 June: 22 had mites. Satisfying and disgusting.

### Winter: oxalic acid

Done when the hives are broodless, late December, by vapour this time rather than trickling. The method, doses and the business with the mask are all in [[Oxalic acid vapour dosing]]. Before that I trickled Api-Bioxal in December 2023, 5 ml per seam of bees, and it worked but the bees didn't love it.

## Results after treatment

Drop counts in the 7 days after the vapour on 28 December 2024: Hazel 412, Primrose 238, Bramble 97, Ivy 31. Then down to single figures a day by mid January. All four came through winter, see [[Winterizing the hive]].

## Things to remember

- Rotate treatments, don't use amitraz every year, resistance
- Write the batch number and dates on the record card ([[Hive inspection checklist]]) and in the Veterinary Medicines Record book, it's the law
- Never treat with supers on
- Hazel's queen should probably be replaced in 2025, her stock seems to tolerate mites less well
